subject: §PERF-MIRROR-BATCH decision — is batch-bracketing the authoritative mirror a real browser target?
environment: Windows 11, node v24.15.0, tsx, headless (no THREE, no render); real WallStore + real wireAuthoritativeElementMirror + real storeEventBus

1_mirror_headless.note: reproduces the BASE-INNER attribution — the mirror does all 1000 add()s because the headless harness never wires the L7 §P2.1 bridge

2_mirror_browser.note: §P2.1 bridge pre-added all 1000 first (as it always does in the browser); every mirror getById() hits -> skip. THE MIRROR PERFORMS ZERO add()s.

4_fanout_batched.note: storeEventBus.batch() BUFFERS then flushes all N deliveries at endBatch — it does NOT reduce total subscriber work and can add buffering overhead; batching here is a jank/longtask fix (endBatchYielded), NOT a throughput lever

verdict: CONFIRMED NO-OP — §PERF-MIRROR-BATCH on packages/runtime-composer/src/authoritativeElementMirror.ts saves ~0 browser milliseconds. The 228ms->(post-2a)~44ms the inner harness attributes to the mirror is paid in the browser by the L7 §P2.1 bridge's own WallStore.add(), whose store-internal cost was already flattened by fix 2a. Adding a batch bracket to a provably-dead code path is pure risk with no benefit.
redirect: The per-add browser cost is genuine once-per-element work (store-internal [flattened by 2a], VDT/bimManager register, subscriber processing) that must happen per wall regardless. No throughput win exists from batch-bracketing EITHER the mirror OR the storeEventBus fan-out (arm 3 vs 4). The only remaining lever is longtask/jank, already owned by BatchCoordinator.endBatchYielded (200 events/frame).
falsification: arm 2 asserts adds-performed === 0 (invariant across runs), not merely 'fast'.
